project: Conan — v4.6: HUD polish, fixable MCP, editable Settings, responsive bottom-dock, and Appearance (fonts + themes)
description: Polish + extend the Conan HUD/observation surface and make it personalizable. Two real bug fixes (Pulse dark-mode X-axis legibility; redundant Timeline × close button), HUD secondary-toolbar unification (Pulse + Usage join Skills/MCP), the full /usage stats surfaced (contributing-factors insights + per-skill % — already buffered, just dropped), one-click MCP authenticate/reconnect (driving the /mcp TUI via a throwaway pty, since `claude mcp` has no auth subcommand), an editable Settings dialog (drop search, real tabs, Status rows become editable reusing the existing config-write path), a responsive bottom-dock HUD at narrow widths (replacing the auto-hide), and an Appearance Settings tab (terminal mono-font picker via curated-list + canvas detection because queryLocalFonts is Chromium-only/unavailable in macOS WKWebView; plus multiple themes from a ~/.conan/themes.json config file applied over the ~20 :root CSS tokens). Source: docs/v4.6-prd.md (compiled from docs/v4.6-backlog.md). Sequencing: quick bugs (F3/F6) → HUD toolbar (F2) → Usage stats (F5) → MCP auth (F1, spike first) → Settings chain (F4→F8→F9) → responsive (F7, largest). Build stays green at every story.

userStories.title: Responsive: min-size enforcement + short-window guard
userStories.description: As a Conan user on a small window, I want the bottom HUD to never collapse into an unusable sliver, so the layout stays usable.
acceptanceCriteria: A useWindowHeight hook (sibling to useWindowWidth) provides the live window height
Terminal and HUD minimum heights are enforced in the bottom-dock layout so neither region collapses
Below a window-height floor, the bottom HUD is clamped (or kept toggleable via the View ▸ HUD menu) rather than rendered as an unusable sliver — the menu toggle remains the escape hatch
Switching wide↔narrow restores each dock's last size
Verify in browser using automate-browser skill at narrow+short, in both light and dark mode (no unusable sliver; sizes restore per orientation)
cd ui && npm run build is clean
Typecheck passes
